title: Observational Indistinguishability and Integrity Blind Regions in Hybrid Quantum-Classical Workflows
description: Version 1.3.2 reproducibility artifact of Paper 1.5. This controlled methodological/editorial correction leaves the experimental evidence frozen at version 1.3.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22648573): no experiment, job, model, kernel, attack, seed, dataset or draw was rerun. The sensor audit establishes that the selected Class-A sensors execute statistically thresholded aggregate comparisons against a benchmark-protected clean same-item-set oracle without item pairing; this is neither a purely historical reference nor demonstrated deployed authentication. Classes B and C are trusted same-batch exact invariants at aggregate and item-aligned granularity. Frozen-output-derived additions report the complete sensor-to-reference mapping, the trusted near-null cost (85 gross exact blocks, 46 overlapping batch interruptions, 39 net additional interruptions out of 1,200), and adaptive materiality/detection/served rates at every preregistered strength. The paper foregrounds minimum evidence granularity relative to the protected integrity claim, uses materially altered audit result served for the internal unsafe_allow endpoint, defines tau to zero-plus as structural sensitivity, distinguishes row counts from clustered inferential units and exact-zero from clean-decision denominators, restores contiguous Corollaries 1--3, and bounds the quantum branch to ideal-statevector and finite-shot emulation. Contents include code, tests, eight SHA-256 evidence manifests, compact derived evidence, figures, formal core, amendment audit, adversary model, manuscript sources and submission PDFs.
